messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] sev2 detected: elevated OOM rate on serving-runtime cluster us-east-1 (pool: dedicated-gpu-02). 23 failures in 5m, GPU OOM + CUDA errors. Auto-created incident channel | https://ops.redwood.example/alerts/1719854321

maria_s: oncall here, pulling logs and metrics now.

rahul_m: tailing node logs, seeing repeated CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS and allocation failures: 'cuMemAlloc failed: out of memory' interleaved with lots of small page allocations. Attaching small snippet.

rahul_m: ```
[2026-03-17T21:12:03Z] ERROR serving-runtime: cuda_runtime_api.cc:47 cuMemAlloc failed: out of memory
[2026-03-17T21:12:04Z] WARN kvcache: page_alloc: created fragment id=0x4f3 len=12KB total_frag=987
[2026-03-17T21:12:04Z] INFO allocator: resident=14.2GB rss_growth=+120MB
```

jeff_k: CS report: several customers (notably AcmeCorp) seeing timeouts/5xx for embeddings and chat endpoints. Metrics show 2% org-wide errors, AcmeCorp ~12% over last 10m. CS opened ticket #4321.

sre_lisa: can we short-circuit to smaller model variants or route some traffic off this pool while we triage?

maria_s: immediate mitigations: 1) lowering batch_size via FF and 2) pinning heavy sessions to quantized fallback. Pushing flag now.

maria_s: ```bash
# apply immediate flag to reduce batch pressure
curl -X POST "https://admin.redwood.example/api/flags" -d '{"key":"batch_size_override","value":"1","scope":"us-east-1"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx'
```

eng_runtime_bot: started job restart-pod-serving-47 (job id: jr-8812) to reclaim memory on affected pods.

rahul_m: restarted pod but node flapped twice within 3m. After restart, RSS climbs slowly again — looks like allocator microfragmentation + KV cache growth on long-lived sessions. Small anonymous mappings pile up and aren't reclaimed.

maria_s: applying traffic-shift: move 15% of live inference traffic from us-east-1 to us-west-2 via smart-routing policy. Command: `routectl set-policy --shift 15 --from us-east-1 --to us-west-2`

jeff_k: done. Routing change observed in metrics, tailing latencies now.

rahul_m: attempting targeted KV compaction on node serving-023: `/opt/redwood/bin/kvctl compact --node=serving-023 --force` — kicked off, reporting progress.

customer_success: note from AcmeCorp: "We're seeing intermittent failures on embeddings in our daily batch jobs. This started ~20m ago. Any ETA?" Ticket #4321 updated.

maria_s: quick impact summary: org-wide 2% request failure rate, specific customer AcmeCorp seeing 12% errors. Root cause hypothesis: paged-attention allocator microfragmentation interacting with KV cache retention for long sessions; memory slowly creeps until CUDA allocation fails and container crashes.

maria_s: immediate action plan:
1) Mitigate: restart affected pods + traffic shift to reduce pressure (done).
2) Short-term patch (hrs): force KV eviction on idle sessions, cap per-session KV pages (set limit 8MB), lower max_concurrent_requests per node to 8.
3) Mid-term (days): allocator metadata compaction + improve slab reuse heuristics.
4) Long-term (weeks): refactor paged-attn allocator to reduce fragmentation and add background compaction and better accounting.

sre_lisa: applying max_concurrent_requests=8 on pool now. Expect lower throughput but better stability.

maria_s: set `max_concurrent_requests=8` and enabled `kv.evict_on_idle=true` with `kv.evict_idle_seconds=60` on the affected pool. Canary rolling to all dedicated nodes.

rahul_m: logs after kv-evict shows fewer page fragments being retained, resident memory growth slowed. Still watching for regressions.

rahul_m: ```
[2026-03-17T21:18:30Z] INFO kvcache: evict_on_idle triggered for session=0x9b3 idle=62s freed=2.4MB
[2026-03-17T21:19:10Z] INFO allocator: resident=12.6GB rss_growth=+12MB/10m
```

eng_runtime_bot: canary patch deployed: `kv-evict` enabled on `dedicated-gpu-canary` pool. Monitoring telemetry for 30m.

jeff_k: CS: AcmeCorp updated that errors dropped to ~6% after routing change. They're asking for an ETA on full remediation.

maria_s: ETA: short-term config changes should stabilize in 1–3 hours, mid-term allocator work needs eng-runtime owner and will take days. Assigning to @rahul_m and @eng_runtime for root cause fix.

maria_s: handing off to night oncall @jeff_k — checklist below. Posting handoff: please monitor memory RSS per pod (alert threshold: >13.5GB), watch node flaps (>2 within 10m => escalate), keep traffic shifted until stability confirmed, and update CS on progress and ETA.

maria_s: handoff checklist:
- watch: pod RSS, GPU OOMs, CUDA errors
- actions: restart pod if RSS > 13.5GB and not responding to kv-evict
- escalate: if OOM persists after 3 restarts or node flaps, page SRE lead and open a P0 page
- customer comms: ensure CS posts hourly updates to AcmeCorp and includes mitigation steps

jeff_k: acknowledged, taking over monitoring. I'll keep this thread updated and post a summary to #incidents-summary once stable. :white_check_mark:
